video.title: The Easiest Way to Make Money With AI Right Now

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Aaron Edwards, founder of DocsBot, an AI customer support agent SaaS that passed $1M ARR in 3.5 years with >90% gross margin, ~$130 ARPU and ~3% revenue churn. After several failed AI image products, he built DocsBot from a problem at his employer, launched via build-in-public on Twitter, and now sells mostly through agencies that charge small businesses about $2,000-$3,000 setup and $500/month. He describes an automated pipeline: find businesses with docs but no chatbot (BuiltWith, job posts), auto-build a demo bot, and send AI monthly reports. Key takeaway: the opportunity is implementing AI agents for businesses that won't do it themselves.

tactics.name: Automated AI-agent sales pipeline
steps: Use ChatGPT/Claude ($20/month) with tools to find businesses with a knowledge base/docs but no chatbot
Use BuiltWith to list sites using basic widgets like Help Scout
Scrape job sites/LinkedIn for companies hiring support agents (budget ready)
Find decision-maker contact via Tregt (API router to Apollo etc., ~1c/lead)
Auto-build a bot on their docs via DocsBot MCP and send a demo link
Charge ~$2,000 setup + $500/month

quote.text: Go find businesses, manufacturers that are doing this and that have a knowledge base on their website, but no chatbot
quote.speaker: Aaron Edwards

tactics.name: Automated monthly value report
steps: Each month have AI analyse the client's bot logs and stats
Generate branded PDF report and email it
Flag unanswered questions and recommend new support docs

quote.text: For that 500 bucks a month, it's doing it for you
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: 10x value pricing
steps: Estimate tickets/month and minutes per ticket
Assume conservative deflection (50%)
Show savings ~10x the fee

quote.text: you want to provide 10 times the value that you charge
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Paid-first instead of free trial
steps: Require payment upfront with refund guarantee
Filters for serious customers and saves founder time

quote.text: you pay us and show us you're serious. We'll give you a refund if it doesn't work for you
quote.speaker: Aaron Edwards

tactics.name: Waitlist + survey MVP
steps: Share concept with your network
Waitlist form plus survey on core features
Build the minimum feature set in two weeks

tactics.name: Conference attention hack
steps: Skip $25k booth

Walk the floor

tactics.name: Solve your employer's problem first

Make them first customer while transitioning out

warnings.warning: Viral free products don't mean revenue.
Self-serve SaaS demand from tech-savvy customers has dried up; need service/implementers.
Underpricing: his son wanted to charge $500/month for $100k/year value.
Cheap outreach (cold email, LinkedIn DMs) is increasingly ineffective.

warnings.warning: Fads die; AI profile pictures revenue disappeared.

lessons.lesson: Try many cheap experiments while employed; the ninth stuck.
Build in public: one repost from a stranger can launch a product.

quote.text: all it takes is one dude in Japan
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Charge more than you think; offer high tiers and enterprise contact.

quote.text: charge more than you think you should
quote.speaker: Aaron Edwards

lessons.lesson: Bad-fit customers (solo devs) churn and DIY; target companies with support teams.
SMBs won't learn new software; the opportunity is implementation services on top of AI.

quote.text: They're installing water heaters. Yeah. Exactly. So they need that person

lessons.lesson: Companies hiring support staff already have budget and ticket load.
Spend more per prospect on unique outreach when deal value is high.
Lifestyle bootstrapping gives freedom (6 weeks vacation) but slower growth; he'd reinvest more in ads.
Prove value monthly to justify retainers.
